content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To go to college after high school, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Request official high school transcripts (1 week)
Step 2. Register for the SAT or ACT (30 minutes)
Step 3. Research potential university majors (4 hours)
Step 4. Write the first draft of the personal statement (3 days)
Step 5. Attend a local college fair (3 hours)
Step 6. Discuss college budget with parents (2 hours)
Step 7. Create a list of reach and safety schools (5 hours)
Step 8. Obtain a letter of recommendation from a science teacher (2 weeks)
Step 9. Submit the final Common Application (1 hour)
Step 10. Pay the application processing fees (15 minutes)
Step 11. Complete the FAFSA financial aid form (2 hours)
Step 12. Submit the mid-year grade report (20 minutes)
Step 13. Brainstorm extracurricular activity descriptions (2 hours)
Step 14. Mail a portfolio of artwork (4 days)
Step 15. Proofread the final essay for typos (2 hours)
Step 16. Verify receipt of all application materials (30 minutes)
Step 17. Schedule an alumni interview (1 hour)
Step 18. Update the counselor on the final school list (30 minutes)
Step 19. Receive and review financial aid award letters (1 week)
Step 20. Take a virtual campus tour (1 hour)
Step 21. Ask a counselor for a fee waiver (20 minutes)
Step 22. Compare different campus housing options (3 hours)
Step 23. Study for subject-specific placement tests (10 hours)
Step 24. Create a student portal account for each college (2 hours)
Step 25. Finalize the choice of a specific college (2 days)
Step 26. Draft a resume of high school achievements (3 hours)
Step 27. Submit a housing preference form (45 minutes)
Step 28. Visit the campus in person (1 day)
Step 29. Gather parent tax return documents (1 week)
Step 30. Pay the non-refundable enrollment deposit (10 minutes)
Step 31. Register for freshman orientation (30 minutes)
Step 32. Sign up for a college-specific email address (15 minutes)
Step 33. Browse the course catalog for the first semester (3 hours)
Step 34. Check for any required health immunizations (1 hour)
Step 35. Order a final high school transcript after graduation (15 minutes)
Step 36. Buy a new laptop for school (2 hours)
Step 37. Take the SAT or ACT exam (4 hours)
Step 38. Send official test scores to the admissions office (20 minutes)
Step 39. Ask a mentor to review the college list (2 hours)
Step 40. Write a thank-you note to the recommendation writers (30 minutes)
Step 41. Complete a summer reading assignment (10 hours)
Step 42. Attend a regional "meet and greet" for new students (2 hours)
Step 43. Apply for local community scholarships (1 week)
Step 44. Review the student code of conduct (1 hour)
Step 45. Take a practice standardized test (4 hours)
Step 46. Edit the supplemental essays (5 hours)
Step 47. Attend a workshop on college essay writing (3 hours)
Step 48. Receive the final admission decision letter (2 weeks)
Step 49. Map out the deadlines for all applications (4 hours)
Step 50. Search for college-related social media groups (1 hour)
Step 51. Buy extra-long twin sheets for the dorm (1 hour)
Step 52. Research local banks near the campus (2 hours)
Step 53. Submit the CSS Profile for private institutional aid (3 hours)
Step 54. Register for a college board account (15 minutes)
Step 55. Request a teacher recommendation for the honors program (2 weeks)
Step 56. Apply for a student visa if studying abroad (1 month)
Step 57. Calculate the total cost of attendance (2 hours)
Step 58. Compare meal plan options (1 hour)
Step 59. Look for a part-time campus job (3 hours)
Step 60. Finalize the high school senior project (2 weeks)
Step 61. Take an online math placement exam (2 hours)
Step 62. Submit the final enrollment contract (10 minutes)
Step 63. Review the student health insurance plan (1 hour)
Step 64. Join the official freshman Facebook group (15 minutes)
Step 65. Clean out the high school locker (1 hour)
Step 66. Fill out the emergency contact form (15 minutes)
Step 67. Narrow down the college list to ten schools (5 hours)
Step 68. Attend a high school graduation ceremony (3 hours)
Step 69. Create a common app account (20 minutes)
Step 70. Draft a list of questions for the admissions officer (1 hour)
Step 71. Take a required online alcohol awareness course (2 hours)
Step 72. Review the credit transfer policy for AP classes (2 hours)
Step 73. Sign the federal student loan master promissory note (30 minutes)
Step 74. Research student organizations and clubs (3 hours)
Step 75. Discuss potential majors with a guidance counselor (1 hour)
Step 76. Submit a final immunization record (20 minutes)
Step 77. Check the college's early decision deadline (10 minutes)
Step 78. List hobbies and interests for the application (1 hour)
Step 79. Attend an admitted students day event (6 hours)
Step 80. Review the campus map and building locations (1 hour)
Step 81. Take a campus tour of the local state school (2 hours)
Step 82. Write a letter of interest to a waitlist (2 hours)
Step 83. Select a move-in date and time slot (15 minutes)
Step 84. Apply for a parking permit if bringing a car (30 minutes)
Step 85. Look up average GPA requirements (1 hour)
Step 86. Request a recommendation from the English teacher (2 weeks)
Step 87. Send a mid-year grade update to colleges (15 minutes)
Step 88. Organize all college documents into a folder (1 hour)
Step 89. Receive the financial aid package notification (1 week)
Step 90. Decline offers from schools not being attended (30 minutes)
Step 91. Research the weather in the college town (1 hour)
Step 92. Take a career aptitude test (1 hour)
Step 93. Discuss the possibility of a gap year (2 hours)
Step 94. Set up a meeting with the financial aid office (1 hour)
Step 95. Buy a specialized planner for the school year (30 minutes)
Step 96. Draft a preliminary college budget (2 hours)
Step 97. Confirm the final financial aid package (30 minutes)
Step 98. Obtain a copy of the high school diploma (1 week)
Step 99. Submit the final housing deposit (15 minutes)
Step 100. Choose a roommate through the online portal (2 hours)
